intro: Analytics ka kaam numbers ko decision me badalna hai. Is section me CSV data load karna, groups banane, percentages, top-N, moving average, date grouping aur export — poora reporting pipeline pure Python me practice hota hai, jo Power BI ke visuals ke peeche bhi chalta hai.
theory: Report ka pehla sawaal grain hai: ek row kis cheez ko represent karti hai? Grain clear hone se hi totals/percentages sahi hote hain.
Percentage ka denominator explicitly choose karo — total rows, total sales ya filtered subset? Galat denominator sabse common analytics bug hai.
Grouping ke baad sorting/top-N se story nikalti hai; raw totals se bade numbers aate hain par priority nahi.
Moving average noise smooth karta hai; window size chhota ho to responsive, bada ho to stable — trade-off report ke audience par depend karta hai.
Export/refresh reproducible hona chahiye: wahi input, wahi script, wahi numbers. Manual Excel edits version drift laate hain.
syntax:
import csv

with open("sales.csv", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(handle))

from collections import defaultdict

totals = defaultdict(int)
for row in rows:
    totals[row["city"]] += int(row["amount"])

examples.code:
import csv
import io
from collections import defaultdict

raw = '''date,city,amount
2026-01-01,pune,100
2026-01-01,delhi,50
2026-01-02,pune,150
2026-01-02,delhi,50
'''
rows = list(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(raw)))

city_totals = defaultdict(int)
day_totals = defaultdict(int)
for row in rows:
    amount = int(row['amount'])
    city_totals[row['city']] += amount
    day_totals[row['date']] += amount

grand = sum(city_totals.values())
print('city share:', {city: round(v / grand * 100, 1) for city, v in city_totals.items()})
print('daily:', dict(sorted(day_totals.items())))
print('top city:', max(city_totals, key=city_totals.get))
explain: Ek hi pass me city totals, daily totals aur shares — report ka core aggregation.
Ye snippet end-to-end flow dikhata hai.
Output ko project/interview me evidence ki tarah use karo.

realWorld: Sales dashboards me city/product wise revenue, share aur growth rate standard KPIs hain; denominator missing hone se share 100% cross kar jata hai.
Daily data ka 7-day moving average ops reviews me noise kam karta hai.
Power BI/Tableau ka data model bhi wahi groupby/join logic hai — Python me samajh lo to DAX/M ke concepts aasan ho jate hain.

interview.q: Report me grain ka matlab kya hai?
interview.a: Ek row kis entity/level ko represent karti hai — order, customer, city-day. Grain mix hone se double counting hoti hai; totals se pehle grain statement likhna chahiye.

interview.q: Percentage ka denominator kaise choose karte hain?
interview.a: Sawaal se: "total revenue me share" ke liye overall total, "city ke andar product share" ke liye city total. Denominator explicitly document karo.

interview.q: Moving average aur simple average me kab kya?
interview.a: Trend dekhna ho to moving average (noise smooth), overall level chahiye to simple average. Window size report ki cadence se match karo.

interview.q: Dashboard number aur raw query number mismatch kyun hote hain?
interview.a: Filters, date ranges, duplicate rows, ya grain ka farq. Dono taraf ka denominator aur filter explicitly compare karo.

debugging.error: Logic error — sort() None return karta hai, list print nahi hoti
debugging.why: sort() in-place hai aur None deta hai, isliye print None dikhata hai. Ye Data Analytics + Power BI ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: sorted() use karo ya pehle sort phir list print karo.
debugging.lesson: Mutating methods ka return value None hota hai — usse assign/print mat karo.

debugging.broken:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total = p
print(total)
debugging.error: Logic error — total 200 aata hai, sum 300 hona chahiye
debugging.why: Assignment purani value replace karta hai; accumulator chahiye. Ye Data Analytics + Power BI ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: total += p use karo ya sum(prices).
debugging.correct:
prices = [100, 200]
total = 0
for p in prices:
    total += p
print(total)
debugging.lesson: Logic bugs exception nahi dete — chhote sample par expected value likho.

debugging.error: Logic error — pehla do items chahiye the, sirf pehla aaya
debugging.why: Slice ka end exclusive hota hai; 0:1 sirf index 0 deta hai. Ye Data Analytics + Power BI ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.lesson: Slice boundaries exclusive hoti hain — range jaisa hi rule.

debugging.error: TypeError: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
debugging.why: String concatenation ko dono taraf str chahiye; Python implicit conversion nahi karta. Ye Data Analytics + Power BI ke workflow me bhi wahi galti hai.
debugging.fix: f-string ya str() se explicit conversion karo.
debugging.lesson: TypeError type mismatch batata hai — conversion explicit karo.
